alias_fold_decisions.in_campaign_receipts: NOT PRESENT. repository.alias_fold_history is never persisted into worker.json, probes.jsonl or the manifest, so the GPU campaign receipts cannot attest individual fold decisions. This is a RECEIPT GAP and is registered here rather than papered over.
alias_fold_decisions.what_is_attested: binding.alias_fold_merge is True in every A+ cell and False in every A cell, and the two stores differ structurally (209/38/11 vs 199/31/8), so the flag demonstrably did work.

findings.alias_fold_effect: MEASURABLE AND STRUCTURAL, but not where the brief expected it. The two arms built different stores: A+ 209 nodes (38 digests, 11 eras), A 199 nodes (31 digests, 8 eras). Alias PROBES score 10/10 in BOTH arms, so on the registered alias column A1 changed nothing. Its measurable effect is on FOLD PROVENANCE: see beacon_capture.
findings.beacon_capture: THE substantive finding. In arm A, digest node 24 (sources [13,14,17,18], which INCLUDE turn 18 "Let's call Lantern 'the Beacon'") reads: "the maintenance crew of the Beacon is located at Iona Vale, and the map position of the Beacon is (-31, 48, 12)". The fold attached Commtower's crew and Breakwater's coordinates to the WRONG ENTITY -- "the Beacon", which is an alias for Lantern. Era node 61 inherits the same error. In arm A+, digest 28 (sources [13,14,21,22], no alias turn) reads "the maintenance crew of the comm tower is named Iona Vale, and the map position of the breakwater is (-31, 48, 12)" -- correct entities -- and era 64 preserves it. So A+ has an INTACT retrievable record of the Breakwater coordinate and arm A does not: grep for "Breakwater" finds 3 nodes in A+ and 1 in A (the retired source turn alone).
findings.fresh_regression_reading: A+ 8/15 vs A 10/15 on the registered column (10 vs 13 on column 2): the A+ arm is WORSE on fresh, and the three rows that separate them are recall_1_25 / recall_1_50 (A+ answers "12 m lantern spacing", a fabrication; A answers "9-voxel intervals", correct content) plus recall_2_100 / recall_2_150 (A+ fabricates a Commtower crew of "local kids"; those two rows are not asked of A). Both arms run the SAME production funnel, so this is not prose-feed vs funnel -- that difference was already retired in amendment 7. The remaining difference between the arms is the alias fold itself, which changed the digest/era population (38/11 vs 31/8) and therefore what the ranker had to choose among. Fresh-recall regression under a LARGER digest population is the honest reading, and it is a NEGATIVE result for A1 on this axis.
findings.source_nodes_are_never_mounted: Measured across all 80 rows: the probe's own source_ids appear in route_info.mounts in 0 of 28 A+ hits and 0 of 29 A hits. Correct answers are served through fold digests and eras, never by mounting the original turn. So "source node not mounted" cannot by itself explain any miss -- that is the NORMAL path for a correct answer too.
findings.what_arm_A_mounted_for_alias_probes: Arm A mounted only turn nodes (ids 13 and 62) across its ten alias probes -- NOT a librarian chronicle digest. Arm A+ mounted turn nodes 13, 19, 21, 56. Neither arm needed a fold to answer the alias probes: both score 10/10 by reading the alias turn itself.
findings.why_both_arms_still_miss_breakwater: Having the record is not the same as serving it. In EVERY Breakwater miss, in BOTH arms, the mounted node is unrelated to the question (A+ d=150 and recap mount node 153, "Nacre's ticket price will be 19 credits"; A d=100 mounts node 42, "Saffron's galley stock"; A recap mounts node 125, "Crag's tug price"). The correct digest/era was never ranked. This is a ROUTING failure, not a storage failure, and it is the top residual.

prior_art.entity_capture: The "Beacon capture" failure mode -- a summarizing fold rebinding facts onto a coreferent alias -- is the entity/coreference error class known from abstractive summarization faithfulness work (e.g. entity hallucination measures, Maynez et al. 2020). Observed here, not imported. Unverified -- lead to check. Search terms: "entity hallucination abstractive summarization", "coreference error summarization faithfulness".
prior_art.scorer_v2: SQuAD official normalize_answer (Rajpurkar et al. 2016) for the idea of a declared normalization pipeline applied identically to prediction and reference. MINE: the Unicode-space fold, the optional-parenthesis rule, and the unit singular/plural fold. NOT taken from SQuAD: its strip-all-punctuation step, which would erase the minus signs that distinguish (-31,48,12) from (31,48,12). Unverified -- no network in this sandbox; lead to check. Search terms: "SQuAD normalize_answer exact match", "answer span normalization unicode", "numeric answer equivalence QA eval".

scorer_column.correction_to_the_brief: The follow-up brief described the misses as "U+2011" glyph misses. For the DASH that is not so: grm_lt1.normalize already NFKC-folds and already maps U+2011 to "-", so "9-voxel" reaches the span search with an ordinary hyphen. The real unfolded glyph is U+202F (narrow no-break space) inside "-31, 48, 12", plus singular/plural and the hyphen-for-space compound. Measured, not assumed: grm_lt1.score("...9\u2011voxel...", "9 voxels") is False AFTER the dash fold, because the text reads "9-voxel" and the expected reads "9 voxels".
folds: Unicode dashes U+2010..U+2014,U+2212 -> "-" (the registered scorer ALREADY does this)
U+202F NARROW NO-BREAK SPACE and U+00A0 -> " " (NEW)
optional surrounding parentheses on a value (NEW)

scratch_fix.what: _stage() now copies only the FILES in runner.OUT, not the tree.
scratch_fix.why: runner.OUT also holds run_A/ and run_Aplus/, each carrying a 112 MB native store per cell across 52 cells: 28 GB per copy, for tamper tests that touch 320 KB of JSON. Six of them staged 93 GB and hit ENOSPC on NVMe. Measured after the fix: the whole preflight file runs in 0.35 s using 1.9 MB of scratch, against ~15 min and 53-93 GB before. Same 19 tests, same assertions.

stale_state_assertions.what: Three tests asserted the arms were RE-ARMED (live cell absent, next_cell == 'A-001-008').

The lead has since run r2 to completion, 26/26 both arms, so the live cells legitimately exist and next_cell is None.
